_meta.description: Structured corpus of IMW Stage One Assessment (S1A) PRACTICAL papers, 2015-2026. A difficulty-calibrated sibling of data/exams.json: one 12-wine blind-tasting paper per year, written by the same examiner panel one step below the stage-two exam. Theory questions are NOT captured here (see docs/s1a_papers/ for the full papers).
_meta.source: docs/s1a_papers/*.pdf (downloaded from mastersofwine.org 2026-08-05; see outputs/imw_website_crawl_2026-08-05.md for URLs). 2021-2023 PDFs have no text layer; their entries were transcribed from rendered page images.
_meta.conventions: Question text and wine full_text are transcribed verbatim from the papers (line-wrap artifacts joined; original misprints preserved and flagged in notes). Marks per year sum to 300 (25/wine average), validated by scripts/validate_s1a.py.
_meta.gap_note: No S1A in 2020 (pandemic). 2021 was sat remotely: Q1 was a 'dry note' question with the wines disclosed in the stem, and the wine list covers slots 3-12 only.

questions.text:
Wines 1-2 are sparkling.
For each wine:
a) Identify the origin and grape variety/ies as closely as possible. (2x10 marks)
b) Comment on the method of production. (2x8 marks)
c) Comment on the quality and maturity. (2x7 marks)

Wines 3-6 are made from different single varieties.
For each wine:
a) Identify the variety and origin as closely as possible. (4x13 marks)
b) Assess the quality and style of the wine, making reference to its likely commercial position. (4x12 marks)

Wines 7-10 are made from the same single variety and come from three different countries.
For all four wines:
a) Identify the grape variety. (12 marks)
Then for each wine:
b) Outline the commercial potential. (4x4 marks)
c) Identify the origin. (4x7 marks)
d) Comment on the winemaking. (4x4 marks)
e) Comment on the quality and maturity. (4x7 marks)

Wines 11-12 are from the same country and region.
a) Comment on the wines as a pair, making reference to their region of origin, quality, winemaking, maturity, ability to age and commercial appeal. (50 marks)

Please write dry note answers for this question using the following information:
Wine 1: Cava Gran Reserva Brut Nature 2015. 55% Xarel-lo, 35% Macabeo, 10% Parellada. 12% ABV, RS <1 g/L. Approximate retail: GBP20-25. Hand-harvested. Cuvée made 100% from free run juice. Second fermentation in bottle, with 36 months on lees prior to disgorgement. No dosage, for Brut Nature style.
Wine 2: Prosecco Treviso DOC Brut NV. 100% Glera. 11% ABV, RS 9-12 g/L, TA 5.5-6.5 g/L. Approximate retail: GBP11. Must is inoculated with cultured yeast for fermentation in stainless steel that results in a base wine of around 9-10% ABV. Wine is transferred into pressurized tanks where it undergoes the Charmat method of secondary fermentation.
